title: Auckland Quiz Night

questions.q: What is Auckland's name in te reo Māori?
Auckland's waterfront and yachting culture have earned it which nickname?
Auckland sits between two harbours. Name either one.
Which symmetrical volcanic island guards the entrance to the Waitematā Harbour?
What is the name of the tall telecommunications and observation tower in Auckland's city centre?
The extra lanes added to the Auckland Harbour Bridge in 1969 were built in Japan. What nickname did they earn?
Which Auckland stadium hosted the Rugby World Cup final in both 1987 and 2011?
Auckland was New Zealand's capital until 1865. Which city took over?
Which singer from Auckland's North Shore had a worldwide hit with "Royals" as a teenager?
The volcanic cone Maungawhau is better known by which English name?

notes: Tāmaki Makaurau is the standard te reo Māori name; see Auckland on Te Ara (teara.govt.nz) or Auckland Council.
Long-standing nickname; see Auckland on Wikipedia or aucklandnz.com.
Waitematā Harbour (east, Hauraki Gulf) and Manukau Harbour (west, Tasman Sea); see Te Ara, 'Auckland places'.
Rangitoto Island, the youngest volcano in the Auckland field; see doc.govt.nz (Rangitoto Island).
Sky Tower opened 1997; see skycityauckland.co.nz or Wikipedia.
Four clip-on lanes built by IHI in Japan, added 1969; see Auckland Harbour Bridge on Wikipedia or NZTA.
Eden Park hosted the 1987 and 2011 RWC finals, both won by the All Blacks; see edenpark.co.nz or world.rugby.
Seat of government moved from Auckland to Wellington in 1865; see nzhistory.govt.nz ('Wellington becomes capital').
Lorde (Ella Yelich-O'Connor), raised in Devonport; 'Royals' released 2013; see Lorde on Wikipedia.
Maungawhau / Mount Eden, one of the Tūpuna Maunga; see maunga.nz or Wikipedia.
